fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from the main driveway.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles on both sides and overhead.
• Clear a turning or staging area near the detached structures so responders can position equipment without blocking the only access point.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of stored equipment or parked vehicles that could block responder movement toward the detached structures.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structures to keep a clear path for responder movement on foot.
• Mark any rear or side gates so responders can locate them quickly without searching.
• Keep rear gates unlocked or secured with a break-away latch to allow responder access from the access drive.
• Identify and mark a secondary foot path to the rear of the property in case the access drive is blocked.
• Cut back vegetation along the sides of the main residence to allow responders to move around the structure without obstruction.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Large Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Green Space; Irrigated Landscape; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly touching or growing against the house on all sides.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove the lowest branches from large trees near the house so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.
• Clear any dead leaves, fallen branches, and dry plant debris that has collected against the house foundation and along the base of walls.
• Separate ornamental shrubs and garden plantings from the house by moving or removing plants placed immediately next to exterior walls.
• Thin scattered trees across the property to reduce the number of connected pathways fire could travel toward the house.
• Keep the single access driveway clear of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate quickly under poor visibility conditions.
• Maintain the irrigated landscape areas close to the house in good condition so vegetation stays green and mowed short.
• Remove any wood piles, outdoor furniture, or other flammable items stored directly against the house exterior.
• Keep grass and low vegetation in the open green space areas mowed short, particularly in areas closest to the structure.
